title: Statutory parameter set for one fiscal year
description: Weights and parameters are DATA, NOT CODE. When the Legislature changes something -- which is near-certain every session -- you edit this file and every calculation, citation and explanation updates. Each entry carries its value, citation, source URL and verified date. A parameter whose citation is not `verified: true` yields null from the engine and marks its computation node unverified; unverified parameters can never silently become published figures.

status.description: `verified` requires every parameter in the file to carry a verified citation. CI enforces this: a file cannot claim verified status while any entry is unverified.

parameters.description: Keyed by dotted parameter name, e.g. `weights.grade.secondary` or `yield.property_dollar_equivalent`.

value.description: Null means not yet verified against current statute text, or not yet set by the Legislature. Null is the honest default and the engine handles it by refusing to produce a number, not by substituting one.

is_law.description: Absent means true: the parameter states what the law says, and its citation is verified by reading the operative sentence in current statute. Set false for a parameter that records what a body PROPOSED and may never enact -- the State Board committee's small/sparse thresholds are the case this exists for. The distinction cannot be left to a reader's inference: quoting a committee report accurately is a different act from quoting a statute accurately, and conflating them is the verification rule's own error running backwards. Anything computed from a parameter with is_law: false must be labelled as measured against a proposed standard.

structural_note.description: What to watch for when reading this one against the source -- specifically where the SHAPE of the calculation, and not just the number, is at stake. Per docs/parameter-verification.md the structural reading is the failure a parameter review is least likely to catch, so the warning belongs beside the parameter rather than in a document nobody opens at the moment of editing.

applies_to.description: Which pupils, districts or towns this parameter applies to, where it is conditional.

range.description: For contingent parameters -- principally the foundation-formula stub, where the Legislature has not acted -- the plausible range instead of a false point estimate. Showing sensitivity honestly beats false precision.

basis.description: Where the range comes from -- a specific bill draft, a JFO scenario, a published consultant recommendation. Never a guess presented as an estimate.

contingent.description: True for parameters of a system the Legislature has not enacted. Everything downstream of a contingent parameter is labelled contingent in the UI.
